review.rationale: Primary material independently challenged for relevance, support, actionable usefulness and limits. Changing documentation is due for re-observation after 90 days; this cadence is review policy, not a guarantee.

reasons.relevance: Owned disposable lifecycles address retained-data safety during database or service trials without implying a current runtime dependency.
reasons.evidence: Official lifecycle and reuse documentation supports stop/removal controls, while isolation still depends on the operator configuration.
reasons.usefulness: The proposed checks identify owned resources, non-default ports, retained-volume exclusions, disabled reuse and verified cleanup.
reasons.clarity: Native temporary-resource workflows remain valid; no Testcontainers execution, speed advantage or automatic isolation is claimed.

need.query: How should I evaluate disposable test dependency lifecycle without risking retained state?

claims.text: Testcontainers documents stop and removal controls, including container-created volumes; reuse and cleanup settings can retain state.

candidates.name: Owned disposable dependency tests
candidates.reason: Keep the current owned disposable lifecycle when sufficient. For a future authorized Testcontainers trial, name one throwaway resource, use a non-default port, exclude retained volumes, leave reuse disabled and assert stop/removal plus preservation of unrelated data. Compare setup/cleanup maintenance with the existing workflow before changing it.
limitations: No library was installed or exercised. Cleanup controls do not prove isolation from retained databases, bind mounts or external effects.

The proposed trial is not an installation or execution instruction for this campaign. Library lifecycle documentation does not establish lower maintenance cost or speed; a native isolated workflow remains a valid choice.
Source-backed advice acquired by the host agent. Local benefit and human usefulness have not been established.
